title: Missing the ability to detect self-inflicted updates
text: Especially when syncing information between an external system and Shopify, I have no idea in webhooks who triggered the update. I have no reliable way of ignoring an update because I know it was me who triggered it. If I can give the mutation (either bulk or separate) a unique identifier, and this identifier would be given in the webhook as well, I could just ignore the webhook with an early return rather than having to do a bunch of calculations and possibly creating infinite update loops between the systems. Bonus points if we can do one of the following: in the mutation specify to ignore create/update webhooks for our own webhook subscriptions specify in the webhook subscription whether or not it should accept webhooks from our own app If I can outright block webhooks triggered by my own app, that would save the Shopify servers some processing as well. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
author: Lynn-srs
triage_reason: Needs a way to identify self-inflicted webhook updates.

title: Export Note component data from Classic app
text: Hi, We’ve moved a classic app, with internal notes, over to a React-based app and would like to bring our notes history with us. The top, solved thread from a user with the same issue indicates that posting a new topic is the best way to get an export of that data, so we can then handle it on our own. So here I am. (Or if there’s a workaround I missed, that would be great to know as well.) Any assistance would be appreciated. Thanks! 4 posts - 3 participants Read full topic

title: Shopify promise and occasional hand delivery
text: I have a few customers who are local to me. Sometimes it makes more sense to arrange hand delivery, especially when I know them personally or want to establish a relationship. (One of them is the clerk at my FedEx store, lol.) Right now I just give them free shipping and drop it off. That kills my Shopify promise rating as there is no tracking information because I don’t buy a shipping label. I don’t want to offer pick-up or local delivery to everyone, but I’d like an honest evaluation of my Shopify promise where these don’t hurt me. I wish there was a way in ADMIN to mark something as local delivery completed so it removes it from the Shopify promise formula. 9 posts - 5 participants Read full topic
author: brassanchordesigns
triage_reason: Local delivery fulfillment ruins Shopify promise tracking metrics.
